subject: [RFC PATCH 13/18] mm/filemap: store the end of a read in f_ra only when it changes

2026-10-19.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the filemap_read function by only updating the f_ra.prev_pos field when the end of a read changes, rather than on every read. This reduces unnecessary cache line bounces and improves performance for threads reading from the same open file. The approach taken is to add a conditional check before updating the prev_pos field.

reviews.author: Linus Torvalds
reviews.summary: Questioned the relevance of the optimization, suggesting it may not be a real-world issue.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, 19 Oct 2026 at 05:50, Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org> wrote:
>
> filemap_read() writes the end of every read to file->f_ra.prev_pos.
> Threads that read through one open file all write that cache line, on
> every read.  The value often stays the same, as for reads that start at
> the same offset each time.

This seems silly. That "often stays the same" is only true for the
pointless benchmark, no?

I don't think it's ever true in any real load.

            Linus

2026-10-20.patch_summary: This RFC patch proposes to optimize the filemap_read() function by storing the end of a read in f_ra only when it changes, reducing unnecessary writes to cache lines.
